title: Plutonium decay half-life activity
learningObjectives: Describe half-life as the time required for a radioactive substance to lose half of its radioactivity, with different isotopes having different half-lives
Calculate the amount remaining after elapsed time using N=N0*(1/2)^(t/T)
Explain that radioactive isotopes transform over time into different isotopes or elements as they decay

explanations.text: A half-life is defined as the time it takes for a radioactive substance to lose half of its radioactivity. Different isotopes of the same element can have very different half-lives, which determines how quickly they decay.

evidence.quote: The different isotopes have different “half-lives” – the time it takes to lose half of its radioactivity.
Pu-239 has a half-life of 24,100 years and Pu-241’s half-life is 14.4 years.

explanations.text: Substances with shorter half-lives decay more quickly than those with longer half-lives, emitting more energetic radiation over the same period. This relationship is modeled by the exponential halving equation.

evidence.quote: Substances with shorter half-lives decay more quickly than those with longer half-lives, so they emit more energetic radioactivity.

explanations.text: Radioactive decay transforms the original isotopes into other products over time. The remaining amount after elapsed time can be predicted from the starting amount and the half-life.

evidence.quote: Like any radioactive isotopes, plutonium isotopes transform when they decay.
They might become different plutonium isotopes or different elements, such as uranium or neptunium.
